sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fleet Route Optimization and Real-Time Telematics SaaS

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 1258 de 2008 (SAS), Código de Comercio arts. 25, 110, 264, 471; Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF); Ley 1121 de 2006; Ley 2010 de 2019 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUB); Decreto 340 de 2020; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1625 de 2016; Circular Única de la Superintendencia de Sociedades (including Circular Externa 10 de 2014); DIAN Resolución 000080 de 2021.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Parent company Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing (if corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Domestic Companies Registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Colombian legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies of all direct and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the UBO's nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation of all foreign incorporation and identification documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Colombia; underlying source documents require prior Apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening against the Colombian UIAF politically exposed persons database, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and domestic Colombian Procuraduría watchlists. Enhanced due diligence is required for non-resident shareholders and for high-risk jurisdictions; customer due diligence under Ley 526 de 1999 and Circular Única of the Superintendencia de Sociedades; identification of ultimate beneficial owners at the 25% threshold through the DIAN RUB database; ongoing monitoring and risk assessment for logistical telematics SaaS with cross-border wire transfers and Stripe billing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) via the respective Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá; portal: https://www.rues.org.co)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be distinguishable in the Roman/Latin script and officially recorded in Spanish. Foreign names or transliterations require a certified Spanish transliteration at registration; only alphanumeric characters and certain institutional tokens are permitted; the suffix 'S.A.S.' is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RUES name-clearing process returns a rejection or a homonymy conflict, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de reposición) before the issuing Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days, and if unsuccessful, a second appeal before the Superintendencia de Sociedades. The applicant may simultaneously request a new name reservation to avoid delays in formation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk logistics-technology SAS as long as the registered address is a determinable physical location inside Colombia where legal notices may be served and file are receivable. A private virtual office or co-working space with permanent mail forwarding is acceptable for back-office/telematics functions, but there must be a physical establishment in Colombia evidencing the commercial substance of the entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: estimated annual probability of 15% for an unannounced on-site inspection by the Cámara de Comercio or tax authority in the first year, with higher risk if the recorded office is only a virtual correspondence address and no clear telematics-related operations are observed.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Código de Comercio and Decreto 19 de 2012

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary and apostille schedule; actual cost varies by document count

UBO pre-registration analysis and RUB filing preparation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for AML/CFT screening packages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUT (Registro Único Tributario) registration with DIAN
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; zero official cost

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), as amended; Código de Comercio arts. 98, 110-112, 353; Decree 1074 of 2015 (RUES); Law 222 of 1995 (commercial oversight).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / Registro Único Empresarial (RUES), under the supervision of the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución e Inscripción en el Registro Único Empresarial (RUES), evidenced by the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum subscribed capital under Ley 1258/2008; payment terms are free but full payment of subscribed capital must occur within two years from incorporation; no bank escrow account is required for cash contributions unless the bylaws impose such mechanism.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the subscription and payment obligations of all shares in the initial capital of the Company be approved as set forth in the incorporation document, and that the share registry reflect each founding shareholder's ownership. FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered office of the Company be established at Calle 93 No. 14-76, Oficina 501, Bogotá D.C., Colombia, and that all corporate purposes be ratified. FURTHER RESOLVED: That [Name] be appointed President and Legal Representative and [Name] be appointed Secretary; both officers, jointly or severally as provided by law, are authorized to execute and file all registrations with the Cámara de Comercio and DIAN, and to retain counsel for corporate governance compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) online portal operated by the Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name through the RUES electronic form; the registry verifies absence of identical or confusingly similar names. Upon clearance, the name is reserved for 30 calendar days. For an S.A.S., the name must include 'S.A.S.' and may be a fantasia name or a reference to the business purpose.
required_dossiers: Request form with at least 5 candidate names
Copy of the requesting founder's citizenship card or passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, re-file with a modified list; if a third-party opposition is raised, present protective arguments to the Cámara de Comercio or appeal to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within 10 calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Private Incorporation Document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública (optional if no in-kind real estate contribution) and all founding shareholders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the bylaws, corporate purpose, capital subscription and payment schedule, board structure, officers, and audit threshold. All shareholders must execute the document. If any in-kind real estate contribution is included, the document must be elevated to a public deed before a Notaría. Digits with the pre-assigned temporary NIT should be included.
required_dossiers: List of subscribed shares and payment terms
Temporary NIT from DIAN if obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any statutory omission by unanimous written consent of shareholders, re-execute the instrument, and file a corrective amendment with the corresponding notary or Registry if already submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration at the Chamber of Commerce / RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / Registro Único Empresarial (RUES).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed incorporation document, pay the registration fee and the SIC registration tax, and request inscription of the company and its legal representative. Upon successful registration, the authority issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, which constitutes proof of legal existence. After registration, open the corporate books and register with the Chamber's Certified Public Accountant office if required.
required_dossiers: Private incorporation document or public deed
Identification of legal representative and acceptance of office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a prevention (obsdervation), file the required corrective document within 10 business days. If denial is maintained, seek an administrative appeal before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio; continued silence is resolved by the applicable legal remedies for expired terms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification and Registration with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), tax administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the company is registered at the Chamber of Commerce, obtain the definitive NIT and complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) through the DIAN online portal. Include the company as an income tax taxpayer, responsible for VAT (if taxable sales exceed the threshold), and select the most common economic activity CIIU 6201 (software development and IT services). Also register with the municipal industria y comercio tax authority in Bogotá as applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Registered office address and public utility bill
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT application is queried, review and correct the information through the DIAN electronic mailbox; submit the required supporting documents and use the formal rectification procedure within the statutory response window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial license is mandated for ISIC 6201 (computer programming and related activities); the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Tourism (MinCIT) is the relevant sector authority for software export benefits, while DIAN remains the regulatory enforcement body.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — Fleet Route Optimization SaaS and Real-Time Telematics software services are subject to free-regime commercial activity under Decree 1074/2015; no manufacturing, technical, or concesión permit is required for the software scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) would only have competency for physical infrastructure projects; for the SaaS scope, the municipal environmental authority of Bogotá (Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente) is the relevant referent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category IV / no mandatory EIA because the registered activity is exclusively software and telematics data processing; no physical premises or industrial discharge are generated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office operations must comply with Bogotá drainage and solid waste rules; no process wastewater or VOCs are emitted. Electrical/electronic waste from servers must be managed under the national WEEE policy (Resolution 1672 of 2013).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the registered office, obtain the fire safety approval from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos de Bogotá when the premises exceed 100 m²; perform structural load inspection for server racks and equipment; issue the Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) program under Resolution 0312 of 2019, and secure the occupational risk insurance enrollment before commencing employee duties.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – portal www.dian.gov.co; transactional portal Muisca for e-filing, RUT and e-invoicing
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must appoint a Colombian legal representative/attorney-in-fact with a notarized power of attorney, prove valid corporate existence, and file the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) with DIAN through the Muisca portal to obtain an NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). Where the vehicle is an S.A.S., the entity is first registered with the local Cámara de Comercio and thereafter obtains and activates its NIT in the RUT with DIAN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no U.S.-style check-the-box election; an S.A.S. is a separate taxpayer. Available elective mechanisms include the 'Régimen Simple de Tributación' (SIMPLES) for taxpayers under the annual UVT threshold, the holding company regime for foreign passive income under Law 2010 of 2019, and contracts for tax stability or megainvestments for qualified projects. Hybrid mismatch rules under Law 2010 and Decree 599 of 2022 govern denial or symmetric treatment of deductible hybrid payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / IVA – Impuesto sobre las Ventas)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic activity threshold applies. Any person performing taxable sales of goods or services in Colombia must register in the RUT as a VAT responsible party before commencing operations. Non-resident digital service suppliers are required to register, charge and remit VAT without any local turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT responsible taxpayers must issue electronic invoices using an DIAN-authorized software provider or DIAN's free electronic invoicing application. Every invoice must include the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) and its XML payload must be transmitted to and validated in real time through DIAN's Muisca WebService (API). Digital certificates (X.509) and SHA-384 signatures are mandated; export invoices require digital stamping and, where appropriate, an electronic 'documento soporte'.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of tangible goods from Colombia to abroad qualifies for the 0% VAT rate upon proving physical departure. Services, including logistics fleet optimization and telematics SaaS, qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is a foreign person not domiciled in Colombia and the service is consumed or used exclusively outside Colombia. The supplier must be VAT registered and maintain contemporaneous evidence of the foreign recipient, service performance, and actual export use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación submitted via MUISCA/SICEX)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / electronic transport document
Commercial invoice and packing list marked 'EXPORTACION'
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas)
Signed SaaS subscription agreement or service contract with foreign counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN will retroactively deny the zero rating, reclassify the operation as subject to 19% VAT, reject all related input VAT refunds and credits, and assess the omitted tax with moratory interest plus the 'sanción por inexactitud' of up to 200% of the understated tax under Articles 648 and 650 of the Tax Code. Fraudulent export documentation can further trigger criminal export fraud proceedings, loss of export incentive status and registration disqualification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia) is the monetary and foreign-exchange authority; the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (MHCP) issues exchange regulations; and the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) acts as the administrative and enforcement body for foreign-exchange controls, money-laundering prevention, and trade-related customs verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a free-market floating exchange rate with full convertibility of the peso (COP) on the country's official exchange market (Mercado Cambiario). Current-account transactions, including service exports, licensing fees, and operational payments, are freely convertible and remittable once properly documented. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment, equity contributions, and cross-border loans, require compliance with Banco de la República's exchange regime, notably the mandatory investment registration and the filing of the corresponding exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio). Profit remittance in the form of dividends is permitted for non-resident shareholders after the applicable withholding tax is settled and the underlying investment is duly registered with Banco de la República; failure to register the foreign investment within the six-month window from the date of disbursement creates administrative penalties and may lead to disallowance of the capital repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombian exchange regulations require all proceeds from the export of goods to be channeled through the foreign exchange market within six (6) months counted from the date of the bill of lading (shipment date). For the export of services, the channeling term is four (4) months from the date of issuance of the corresponding invoice or equivalent receivable recognition. The regulation does not impose a mandatory percentage conversion ratio; rather, it mandates the intermediation of the full export receivable through an authorized foreign exchange intermediary. Exporters may either sell the foreign currency to the intermediate bank at the prevailing representative market rate (TRM) or hold it in an authorized foreign-currency deposit account with a Colombian commercial bank or through a registered cuenta de compensación. All exchange operations must be booked on the corresponding exchange declaration and supported by the commercial invoices, transport documents, tax registry (RUT), and underlying service or sales contracts. Failure to adhere to the timelines may trigger fines and administrative sanctions by the DIAN, and will be considered a foreign-exchange violation under Circular DCIN 83 and Law 9 of 1991.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Caja en Moneda Extranjera

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) and non-bank fintech payment gateways are not authorized to function as deposit-taking entities in Colombia. They cannot issue COP savings or current accounts, cannot clear through the Cámara de Compensación in Colombia, and are not considered valid financial institutions for Colombian exchange-control purposes. Such services may be used only as ancillary payment rails for global disbursement, e.g., paying international cloud vendors or overseas subcontractors, provided the underlying settlement is ultimately routed through a Colombian regulated bank for COP conversion and statutory reporting. Feasibility rating: Medium for outbound vendor disbursements, Low for inbound capital injection and official bookkeeping, because Banco de la República and DIAN treat EMIs as third-party intermediaries and require the underlying bank to retain as the formal counterparty for foreign-exchange reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Colombian SAS with foreign ownership, banks generally require the legal representative or an appointed attorney-in-fact to attend the account-opening interview physically at the bank headquarters or a designated branch. Remote opening is possible only for Colombian resident individuals and very low-risk local corporate structures using the Colombian electronic signature infrastructure, but for non-resident directors, a physical visit, a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, and a videoconference interview with both the compliance officer and relationship manager are mandatory. Certified true copies of the passport, proof of domicile, corporate registry certificate (Cámara de Comercio), SAS bylaws, RUT certificate, and financial statements for the last period are required. Banks may additionally request letters of reference from the beneficial owner's home-country bank and a detailed source-of-funds declaration for any large shareholder contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex non-resident beneficial ownership chain (multi-tier holding, anonymous trust, or legal structure in a lower-tax jurisdiction)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apo-state and apostilled corporate organizational chart showing all underlying shareholders up to the ultimate natural persons; certificate of good standing and articles incorporation for each holding layer; current passport copies of every individual beneficial owner; statement describing the economic activity of the Colombian SAS (fleet dispatch software) with a letter from the allocs accounting firm; and evidence that no nominee shareholders are used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume international software service revenues and irregular inflows to a dormancy soon after bank account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid service agreements executed between the SAS and global logistics clients, including exact deliverables (fleet routing platform licence, telematics data analytics) and negotiated commercial terms; DIAN-issued RUT and electronic invoice resolution demonstrating current operations; bank reference letters from the foreign investor's domicile bank; a detailed waterfall of expected transaction volumes and counterparties; and an explanation of the operational liquidity forecast for the first 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential misclassification as a non-regulated financial or payment institution due to the logistics-technology label and the Saas billing model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Superintendencia Financiera qualification certificate confirming the company is not subject to its authorization and does not qualify as an MSB or PSP; ISIC 6201 classification certificate from the national statistics authority (DANE) and the tax authority; self-reported licensing status confirming no statutory financial licence; whitepaper describing the platform as a software-as-a-service for fleet operators without any handling of transport payments; and a list of current customers and reference to the underlying telematics hardware integration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate inbound equity injection from abroad immediately after account opening with a dormant or inactive balance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital subscription resolutions and a formal company registry act recording the subscribed capital; the shareholder-investment contract; remitter letters signed by the foreign bank authenticating the source of fund; beneficiary identification certificate (NIT) and exact corporate compliance documents; a DAE-validated invoice for the capital contribution if the funds are to be later disbursed for operational expenses; and an explanation of the business purpose for the cross-border cash transfer (e.g., funding initial development and hosting costs).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection must be wired in USD or EUR by SWIFT MT103 from the foreign investor's bank to the Colombian beneficiary SAS account. The wire must clearly identify the beneficiary name, RUT (tax ID) number, and the bank's SWIFT/BIC, and include the remittance information stating 'Foreign Direct Investment – Equity Contribution', referencing the Formulario No. 2 of the foreign-exchange code. The receiving bank will automatically generate a Declaración de Cambio (Exchange Declaration) and register the investment with Banco de la República once the funds are booked. The company's legal representative must ensure the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales (RII) is filed with Banco de la República within the legal term, ideally within 6 months from the date of disbursement, and must retain a notarized copy of the capital subscription minutes, the general ledger entries showing paid-in-capital, and the original account statement trace to the inbound wire. Verification by the bank includes screening of the remitter against OFAC/Banco de la República sanction lists, analysis of source-of-funds for amounts above USD 50,000 equivalent, and an internal anti-money-laundering officer approval for non-resident structures.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade-related disbursements from the Colombian SAS use three primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 international wire transfer for intercompany service fees, vendor payables, software licenses, dividends, and subcontractor payments; these wires require a properly documented underlying invoice and the corresponding bank transaction record to be kept for at least 10 years; (2) commercial letters of credit (documentary LC) for the procurement of physical hardware (GPS terminals, vehicles, signals) when the counterparty insists on a bank guarantee; and (3) global card rails (Visa, Mastercard) for low-value digital subscriptions and recurring SaaS purchases. No letter of credit is required for standard software services and pure intellectual-property payments in the normal course of business. The Colombian bank will only process outbound wires if the corresponding 'Declaración de Cambio' is generated and the supporting documentation is archived, including DIAN invoices where applicable, the service contracts, and tax withholding receipts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forwards (Contratos a plazo) on COP/USD with physical or financial settlement, executed through an authorized domestic financial intermediary and requiring demonstrable underlying exposure
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing the Colombian representative market rate (TRM) for COP/USD, permitted for hedging receivable or payable portfolios without incurring a physical FX exchange
Cross-currency swaps (COP/USD) for durations of one to five years, allowed for qualifying hedging of cash-flow mismatches on long-term international contracts and debt service

Customized currency options (Opciones sobre derivados cambiarios) traded over-the-counter under the supervision of the Superintendencia Financiera, with brokerage only through licensed local banks or foreign banks registered as Colombian market makers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Mercantile Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the company's registered address (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March of each calendar year; for a 31 December fiscal year, renewal is due before 1 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a late surcharge calculated on the registry-renewal tariff; under Article 21 of the Código de Comercio, merchants who fail to renew for 5 consecutive years face cancellation of the mercantile registration and loss of the right to engage in commercial activities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the annual income tax return is due between 20 August and 19 September of the following year, based on the last digit of the NIT under the annual DIAN resolution.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Article 641 of the Estatuto Tributario: 5% of the net tax payable per month or fraction, capped at 100%; if no tax is payable, the penalty is 5% of the larger of gross income or net worth. Failure to file also exposes the company to an official assessment with default interest and administrative collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually under the DIAN calendar, typically mid-February for information corresponding to the preceding calendar year; the exact date depends on the last digit of the NIT.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Articles 651 and 652 of the Estatuto Tributario, failure to file or filing with incorrect information generates penalties calculated as the greater of 1% of the total value of the information required or 5,000 UVT; late-filing penalties accrue monthly and are not related to registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Filing of Certified Financial Statements with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the approval of the financial statements by the shareholders' meeting and no later than the annual mercantile renewal cycle; for a 31 December year-end, the shareholders' meeting must be held by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited or certified financial statements can trigger administrative fines from the Superintendencia de Sociedades and blocks the annual registry renewal; material misstatement may also give rise to corporate and civil liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Registry Update / Confirmation (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero (UIAF) / Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update within 10 working days after any change in beneficial ownership; if there is no change, the registry data must be validated before the annual mercantile renewal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-update or inaccurate beneficial-ownership data is subject to UIAF administrative fines and may cause the company's financial transactions to be blocked or escalated for AML review; no direct registry strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) must appoint a statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) if total assets or gross income exceeds 5,000 times the monthly legal minimum wage (approximately USD 1.6 million in 2024). Appointment is also mandatory if the company is subject to public interest rules or voluntarily elected to have a Revisor Fiscal under its bylaws.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian financial reporting standards based on IFRS: Full NIIF (Group 1) for listed, large, and public-interest entities; NIIF para las PYMES (Group 2) for small and medium-sized entities such as a typical logistics-tech S.A.S.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Colombia does not require a standalone annual UBO declaration; the obligation is satisfied by (i) recording every share transfer in the shareholder ledger, (ii) reporting any change in beneficial ownership to the UIAF within 10 working days, and (iii) certifying the currency of the registered shareholder and beneficial-owner data at the time of the annual mercantile renewal. The shareholders' meeting must also formally approve the annual financial statements and record any resulting shareholder changes in the corporate books.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Minute Book of General Shareholders' Meetings (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)
Minute Book of Board of Directors' Meetings (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Accounting Books (Libros de Contabilidad and Inventario y Balances)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–5,000 per year for a small or mid-size logistics SaaS S.A.S. subject to audit
